note:
The square mana obelisk arrangements with the altar in the middle in 2, 6, and 7 are excellent, but they do not fit in with the identity of a chapel. They all need to have the carpet underneath them made even and symmetrical. Try some other centerpiece objects. separate these rooms into their own category - mana rooms. define them by 1-4 arrangements of mana crystals evenly and symmetrically placed and a wide selection of other arcane objects. 2, 6, and 7 will be given feedback based on their new category (mana room), and their feedback  should not apply to the chapel category. 

all rooms use the same altar - try different objects
Generally, chapels should have a much more symmetric layout.  The carpet that runs down the middle with benches and / or pillars and pews evenly and symmetrically placed on either side and an altar at the end, centered.  

Create an additional separate chapel category for necromancy. call them Covens. Use coffins and sarcophagi and bones, as well as altars, pews, monuments, statues, cauldrons, etc. This is a place where the dead are worshipped and dark necromancy is practiced. many Mana obelisks lining the walls. All of the rules regarding balance and centering of normal chapels should apply to covens as well.  RM-CHAPEL-10 will serve as the basis for the coven category.

Chapels should always be aligned with the main door. The character should walk in and be on the main path facing  the altar.
